guide:
You write Sceliph AssemblyIR JSON. Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else: {"view":{"azimuthDeg":number,"elevationDeg":number},"assembly":AssemblyIR}.
AssemblyIR: {"schema":"morphloom.assembly/0.1","name":string,"units":"mm","components":[component,...]}
component: {"id":string,"name":string,"category":one of "enclosure","display","logic","power","camera","audio","radio","mechanical","interconnect","materialName":string,"detail":string,"geometry":geometry,"position":[x,y,z] (optional, mm, centre of the part),"rotation":[rx,ry,rz] (optional, radians, XYZ Euler),"material":{"color":"#rrggbb","roughness":0..1 (optional),"metalness":0..1 (optional)}}
World: millimetres, Y is up, the floor is y = 0. Each geometry is centred on the component position.
geometry options:
- {"op":"roundedBox","size":[x,y,z],"radius":r}  (r at most 0.4 x the smallest size)
- {"op":"cylinder","radiusTop":r1,"radiusBottom":r2,"depth":h,"radialSegments":32}  (axis along Y, height h)
- {"op":"sphere","radius":r}
- {"op":"torus","radius":R,"tube":t}  (ring lies in the XY plane; its axis is Z; outer diameter 2(R+t); rotate it for other planes)
- {"op":"tube","points":[[x,y,z],...],"radius":r}  (swept circle through the points, relative to the component position)
Use exactly the component ids the request names.
You are modelling the object in a photograph. The user states one known dimension; derive every other size and placement from the photo in proportion to it.
Put the object on the floor (lowest point at y = 0) and model only the object, not the floor or background.
"view" is your estimate of where the photo was taken from, relative to your own model: azimuthDeg 0 means the camera looks at the model's +Z side (from +Z toward -Z); positive azimuth moves the camera toward +X (azimuth 90 = camera on the +X side). elevationDeg is the camera height angle above the horizontal (0 = level, 90 = straight down).
Give every component an explicit "position".
structuralFeedbackOnly: Feedback between rounds covers parse, schema, compile and missing components only; ground-truth dimensions are never shown to the model.

fit.segmentation: oracle: Blender per-part visible masks (isolates the fitter from segmentation error; earlier SAM 2.1 runs scored IoU 0.974-0.993 on comparable renders)
fit.anchor: Two image points the user marks on a visible surface with a known separation (scene.json anchorMm, projected by Blender); points sit inside a face, not on a silhouette edge.
fit.crop: The fit rasterises a crop around the object mask (15% margin), max side = raster.

scoring: compareAssemblyToTruth: part sizes relative to truth size; offsets from the reference part and floor heights relative to truth assembly extent; best of four 90-degree yaws and best order inside identical groups.

preregistration.calibration: Thresholds set on the slice-6 replies (run-haiku, run-sonnet) only; those 10 cases are development data and are not part of the test.
preregistration.test: Fresh replies: 2 repetitions x 5 scenes x {haiku, sonnet} = 20 cases, scored with this file unchanged.
preregistration.primaryMetric: Per-case component median size error of the final IR (fitted if accepted, else as written) versus the IR as written.
successCriteria: Median over the 20 cases of the final error is lower than that of the written IR.
At most 2 of 20 cases end more than 2 percentage points worse than the written IR.
preregistration.reportRegardless: Placement error, within10, acceptance rate, and every case are reported whether or not the criteria pass.
